subject: Combining display and closed storage
hook: The best living-room storage shows off a little and hides a lot. Here is how to get the balance right.
ig:
The best living-room storage shows off a little and hides a lot. Here is how to get the balance right.

Whether it is an alcove unit, a sideboard or a full wall of storage, the same principles apply:

→ Closed low, open high. Cupboards at the bottom handle the heavy and the messy. Display goes at eye level.
→ Decide what earns a shelf. If you would not miss seeing it, it goes behind a door.
→ Use the ledge. Shallower shelves above deeper cupboards leave a handy surface for lamps or drinks.
→ Line it all up. Shelves that follow the door divisions look calm and deliberate.
→ Plan for hosting. Spare glasses, napkins and board games need a closed home near where guests gather.

With the hosting season coming, it is a good week to look at where everything currently ends up.

Save this for your living-room plans, and find our bespoke storage through the link in bio.
fb:
With the festive get-togethers not far off, a lot of us are looking at the living room and wondering where everything is going to go.

The secret to storage that looks good and works hard is the balance between open and closed. Cupboards low down for the clutter and the heavy bits. Shelves at eye level for the things you love. A ledge between them for drinks or a lamp. And a closed spot for the hosting kit: spare glasses, napkins and the board games.
